generated_from: fixed 8+8 register and pinned NOAA/NWS Storm Events bulk CSV releases

dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information; event data supplied through National Weather Service Storm Data
dataset.event_types_included: EVENT_TYPE contains FLOOD, including Flood, Flash Flood, and Coastal Flood variants
limitations: The database covers the United States and adjacent waters; international rows are outside its geographic scope.
Storm Events records are curated significant-event reports and are subject to reporting, timing, and geolocation limitations.

NCEI says events take approximately three months to appear. The pinned 2026 release has flood records through July 31; the August-November portion of the ATLAS window is absent from this downloaded release.

method.geometry: screen each NWS location-table point inside the frozen rectangular AOI bbox; a hit is location context, not an inundation extent
method.time: preserve NWS BEGIN_DATE_TIME and its local CZ_TIMEZONE string; no timezone conversion or OPERA match is asserted
method.deduplication: count unique (year, EPISODE_ID, EVENT_ID); retain distinct LOCATION_INDEX/place/coordinate points within each event

Multiple mPing reports were received, spanning from the north Freeway around Independence Heights to the Sugarland area. Four indicated street flooding with vehicles stranded. One indicated a building had been inundated with water. Additionally, a storm chaser shared a video on social media showing water over the North Freeway frontage Road at West Rocky Creek Road. In the video, one vehicle appears to be stalled out, though others can be seen passing through.

The City of Miami Beach Emergency Manager reported flooding across several roadways in Miami Beach due to heavy rainfall in the area. The South Florida Water Management District estimated 3 to 5 inches of rain in this general area from late October 6th through 7th. Photo evidence showed several inches of rain ponding on the roadways into inclined driveways. Clogged drains may have played a significant role in standing water during this period.

Broadcast media and members of the public reported various instances of flooding in St. Louis County. This ranged from Deer Creek flooding outside of its banks in Town and Country and Shady Grove Creek flooding outside of its banks in Webster Groves. Deep standing water along Wild Horse Creek Road in Chesterfield was also reported due to Wildhorse Creek having risen out of its banks. In Black Jack, Cold Water Creek rose out of its banks as well. Rainfall amounts across the county vary from 2.5 to 6.3 inches ending on April 6th.

An emergency manager reported multiple vehicles trapped in high water on I-70 eastbound under the East Carrie Street overpass. This is a low area. A vehicle was also trapped in flood waters in St. Louis at Lindell Boulevard and Vandeventer Avenue. These areas received between 2 and 4 inches of rain.

Heavy rain caused numerous road closures with vehicles stranded in St. Louis County. Multiple water rescues were reported from cars driving through flooded roadways. At Bayless and I-55, flash flooding from heavy rain and overflow from Gravois Creek resulted in two fatalities.
Heavy rain caused water over major roadways such as I-44 at Nebraska Ave and I-70 at Carrie Avenue. On Skinker Blvd, vehicles were stranded due to flash flooding.
MoDOT reported water over the roadway at northbound I-55 at I-255.

Heavy rain resulted in 15 cars being stranded on I-70 at Saint Louis Ave with the eastbound lane being closed for 30 minutes while firemen worked on clearing drains. Additional street flooding was reported to the west along Saint Louis Ave to Jefferson Ave where 5 to 6 inches of rainwater covered the street. Jefferson Ave was closed at Madison St due to water covering the roadway. To the southeast, water covered the roadway at 13th St at North Tucker Blvd and 13th Street at Cole Street. MoDOT also reported water over the roadway at I-44 and I-64 near the Poplar Street Bridge, though no cars were reported stranded here.
Flash flooding led to the road closures of several interstates including I-44, I-55, I-64, and I-70.

Two of three lanes of I-64 westbound at Forest Park and Hampton became flooded and impassable. Several cars became stuck in flood water. This is a low spot and typically has high water when heavy rain falls.
